config.title: Kita Place in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: When the voucher window opens, which voucher expires, how much licensed capacity is really within a pram walk of your street, what the 30-minute rule means for your claim, and what a Kita is not allowed to charge you.

items.q: How do I get a Kita place in Berlin?
items.a: In two separate steps, and only the first one is the city's job. You apply to the Jugendamt of the district you live in for a Kita-Gutschein, and once it arrives you go looking for a free place yourself and contact Kitas directly. The Senate says this in as many words on its own Kita-Gutschein page. When you find a place you sign a care contract with that provider, the provider reports it to the Jugendamt, and you get written confirmation that the place is financed.

items.q: When can I apply for the Kita-Gutschein?
items.a: At the earliest nine months before you want care to start, and at the latest two months before. Because Kitas run their own waiting lists on their own timetable, the practical move is to apply on the first day the nine-month window opens, and to start ringing Kitas while you are waiting for the voucher to arrive by post.

It depends on the level. A voucher for Teilzeit care of up to seven hours a day does not expire. A Ganztags or extended Ganztags voucher does: under the Kindertagesförderungsverordnung you have to take the place up, meaning sign a care contract, within seven months of the start date the Jugendamt approved. If you let that run out you lose the longer hours you argued for.

items.q: How many hours am I entitled to?
items.a: From your child's first birthday there is a claim to up to seven hours a day and the Jugendamt does not test whether you need it. That is the Teilzeit level. Anything longer has to be justified by work, training or family circumstances. The four levels are 4 to 5 hours Halbtagsförderung, over 5 to 7 hours Teilzeitförderung, over 7 to 9 hours Ganztagsförderung and over 9 hours erweiterte Ganztagsförderung.

A voucher Berlin sends out without being asked. If your child reaches their third birthday without ever having used a Kita-Gutschein, the city posts you a Willkommensgutschein automatically, normally on the condition that you and your child live in Berlin and are registered here. It works like a Kita-Gutschein and is redeemed the same way. Note that it stops being valid if you move out of Berlin.

items.q: How many Kita places are actually near me?
items.a: Far fewer than the number of Kitas suggests. Berlin has 2,917 Kitas holding 200,869 licensed places, but the median Kita is licensed for only 48 children. One in three holds fewer than 30 and that whole third accounts for just 10 per cent of the city's places, while the 744 houses licensed for 100 or more hold 56 per cent. Around the middle of 10247 in Friedrichshain a ten-minute pram walk reaches roughly 40 Kitas and about 2,400 licensed places; across the 190 postcodes in the register the total inside a postcode ranges from 60 places up to 2,953.

items.q: Why are Kitas so much bigger in east Berlin?
items.a: Because they were built next to big housing estates and most of them are still open. The average Kita in Lichtenberg is licensed for 104 children and in Marzahn-Hellersdorf for 100, against 51 in Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf and 57 in Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg. Lichtenberg reaches 18,235 places out of only 175 Kitas, while Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf needs 278 Kitas to reach 14,085. It is worth knowing because a larger house loses a whole cohort to school every August and has to refill it.

items.q: How far away is a Kita place I have to accept?
items.a: Further than most people expect. If you cannot find a place, your district Jugendamt can carry out a Platznachweis listing free and suitable places for you, and those places may be in a neighbouring district. A journey of up to 30 minutes by public transport counts as reasonable. Use that wide radius when you are running out of options, and build your first call list inside the walk you will genuinely repeat twice a day in winter.

items.q: What does a Kita cost in Berlin?
items.a: Attending a Kita or Kindertagespflege in Berlin is free. What you pay is a Verpflegungsanteil of 23 euro a month towards the warm lunch, set by a Kostenbeteiligungsbescheid from the Jugendamt and paid to the provider, and Berlin pays the rest. Breakfast is not inside that funding, so ask each Kita separately. A Halbtagsplatz of four to five hours comes without lunch and therefore without the 23 euro, and the contribution can fall away entirely through the Bildungs- und Teilhabepaket if you receive Grundsicherungsgeld, Sozialhilfe, Kinderzuschlag, Wohngeld or Asylbewerberleistungen.

items.q: Can a Kita charge me extra fees?
items.a: Only within strict limits. Extra payments are always voluntary and only for a genuine additional service you asked for, such as a special organic kitchen. A Kita may not charge for reserving a place, for admission, for a deposit or for cleaning, and forcing you to join a Förderverein is banned. The ceiling is 100 euro per child per month, higher amounts need Senate approval in an exceptional case, and if you decline your contract cannot be terminated for it and your child still takes part in everything.

items.q: What vaccinations and papers does my child need before starting?
items.a: Measles protection is compulsory for a Berlin Kita. A child of two or older needs two measles vaccinations or proof of immunity, a child of one or older needs one, and a child under one needs nothing yet but has to catch up in time. Before care begins you also have to hand in a doctor's Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung and proof of vaccination counselling, both from your paediatrician, so book that appointment when you start calling Kitas.

items.q: Can I move my child to a different Kita and keep the voucher?
items.a: Yes, the voucher carries over, but the funding does not overlap. A new contract can normally only be financed once the old one has been ended, and the notice period under the Kita law may not exceed one month to the end of a month. Only in a genuine hardship case, and where the validity of the notice to the old provider is disputed, can the Jugendamt finance a new contract earlier on a separate application.
